title: Scrambled Brain Pulses Gave 0% Gain, Yet a Custom Rhythm Boosted Memory 37%
description:
In 2018 in the Journal of Neural Engineering, Robert Hampson, Dong Song, Sam Deadwyler, Theodore Berger, and colleagues tested a closed-loop hippocampal memory prosthesis in surgical epilepsy volunteers at Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center and USC. By translating each person's own hippocampal input-to-output timing pattern in real time rather than delivering flat or scrambled electricity, short-term visual matching rose 37% and 75-minute delayed recognition rose 35% (versus 0% under scrambled control pulses).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Hampson RE, Song D, Robinson BS, Fetterhoff D et al. (2018) Developing a hippocampal neural prosthetic to facilitate human memory encoding and recall. Journal of Neural Engineering 15(3): 036014. https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-2552/aaaed7
- Berger TW, Hampson RE, Song D et al. (2011) A cortical neural prosthesis for restoring and enhancing memory. Journal of Neural Engineering 8(4): 046017. https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-2560/8/4/046017
